answer: Fire surprise work bursts: like a comet, a fresh task hits every identity at the same random moment, each needing a few minutes of real reasoning and due within a short window. One operator running 300 fake agents on shared hardware can't finish 300 answers at once, so most clones miss the deadline and forfeit that epoch's reward. The ledger keeps an atlas of who answered on time, and identities that keep timing out together get flagged as one cluster. Accounts may wander between tasks, but only real, separate compute keeps pace.
